provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

glosses: I remember …; I used to … (looking back on the past)
come to think of it, I did …
patterns.usage_note: Recalls past experience aloud, half to yourself, with no answer expected, often with よく and a time frame (あの夏は毎日通ったっけ). The sibling lane is a memory check phrased as a question, put to the listener or to yourself (集合は明日だっけ、鍵を閉めたっけ). It attaches to the plain past, coming out as だっけ after ta-forms that voice た to だ (飲んだっけ) and as たっけ elsewhere.

examples.ruby: そういえば、あの夏[なつ]は毎日[まいにち]プールに通[かよ]ったっけ。
examples.english: Come to think of it, that summer I went to the pool every single day.

examples.ruby: 学生[がくせい]の頃[ころ]は、よく駅前[えきまえ]の古本屋[ふるほんや]に寄[よ]ったっけ。
examples.english: Back in my student days I used to drop by the secondhand bookshop in front of the station all the time.

examples.ruby: 祖母[そぼ]の家[いえ]では、いつも縁側[えんがわ]で猫[ねこ]と昼寝[ひるね]をしたっけ。
examples.english: At my grandmother's house I always used to nap on the veranda with the cat.

glosses: we'd always (do); those were the days when I'd (do)
patterns.usage_note: Looks back on something done again and again over a stretch of past time, usually fondly, so よく and 毎日 sit naturally with it (よく電車に乗って行ったものだ). For a single past experience 〜たことがある is normally the right choice instead. It appears as だもの/だもん after the ta-stems that voice た to だ (泳いだもんだ) and たもの/たもん elsewhere; the excuse-making 〜んだもん is a different construction.

examples.ruby: 子供[こども]の頃[ころ]は、日[ひ]が暮[く]れるまで川[かわ]で泳[およ]いだもんだ。
examples.english: As a kid I'd swim in the river until the sun went down.

examples.ruby: 昔[むかし]の職場[しょくば]では、終電[しゅうでん]まで資料[しりょう]を集[あつ]めたものだ。
examples.english: At my old workplace we'd be digging up material right up to the last train.

examples.ruby: 祖母[そぼ]の家[いえ]までは、よく一人[ひとり]で電車[でんしゃ]に乗[の]って行[い]ったものだ。
examples.english: I used to ride the train out to my grandmother's house all on my own.
